newsitem.title: USA: Epitope faces suit from LA students-lawyers.
newsitem.headline: Epitope faces suit from LA students-lawyers.

text.p: Epitope Inc and its Andrew and Williamson unit face a class action lawsuit filed on behalf of all students in the Los Angeles area exposed to the Hepatitis A virus through contact with contaminated strawberries, the plaintiffs' lawyer said.

The law offices of Greco & Traficante APC said the suit charged defendents with distributing allegedly unsafe, contaminated products that were consumed by Los Angeles area students, exposing them to the virus.
The lawyers said the suit sought just compensation for the students and their parents, as well as punitive damages and a sum sufficient to set up a medical monitoring fund.

Earlier in April, Epitope said its San Diego-based Andrew and Williamson Sales Co unit began a voluntary recall of frozen, sliced strawberries shipped to distributors for institutional use in six states because they were associated with an occurrence of Hepatitis A in some Michigan schools.
Epitope said the berries were grown in Mexico and processed in the United States.
